subject: Environment
description: Covers Kaziranga, Gir, Manas, and Keibul Lamjao.

questions.stem: Kaziranga National Park in Assam is globally renowned for hosting the world's largest population of which endangered animal?

options.option_text: Greater One-Horned Rhinoceros
Asiatic Lion
Bengal Tiger
Snow Leopard

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Kaziranga National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Assam. It is the undisputed global stronghold of the Greater One-Horned Rhinoceros (Rhinoceros unicornis), hosting roughly two-thirds of the world's population. The park's vast expanse of tall elephant grass, marshland, and tropical moist broadleaf forests provides the perfect habitat.
DECOY BUSTING: The Asiatic Lion is found only in the Gir National Park (Gujarat). The Bengal Tiger is widespread but famously associated with Corbett, Ranthambore, and Sundarbans (though Kaziranga also has a very high tiger density). Snow Leopards are found in high-altitude Himalayan parks like Hemis (Ladakh).
EXAM INSIGHT: Kaziranga is crisscrossed by four main rivers, most notably the Brahmaputra. While it is famous for the rhino, it is also a Tiger Reserve and hosts significant populations of wild water buffalo and Asian elephants.

questions.stem: Which National Park in India is the ONLY natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion in the wild?

options.option_text: Gir National Park
Kanha National Park
Bandhavgarh National Park
Ranthambore National Park

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary, located in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat, is the last and only remaining natural stronghold of the Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica). Once roaming freely from the Middle East to Eastern India, their population was decimated by hunting until conservation efforts in Gir saved them from extinction.
DECOY BUSTING: Kanha and Bandhavgarh (Madhya Pradesh) and Ranthambore (Rajasthan) are famous Tiger Reserves. Tigers and lions do not share any natural habitat in India today.
EXAM INSIGHT: Having the entire Asiatic lion population concentrated in one single forest is a massive conservation risk (a single epidemic like Canine Distemper Virus or a massive forest fire could wipe out the entire species). Hence, the Supreme Court has repeatedly ordered the relocation of some lions to Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh to create a second home, though political resistance from Gujarat has delayed this.

questions.stem: Manas National Park, a UNESCO Natural World Heritage site, is located in which state?

options.option_text: Assam
West Bengal
Arunachal Pradesh
Sikkim

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Manas National Park is located in the Himalayan foothills in Assam. It is contiguous with the Royal Manas National Park in Bhutan. It is exceptionally diverse and holds multiple conservation titles: it is a National Park, a Tiger Reserve, an Elephant Reserve, and a Biosphere Reserve.
DECOY BUSTING: West Bengal hosts Jaldapara and Buxa. Arunachal has Namdapha. Sikkim has Khangchendzonga.
EXAM INSIGHT: Manas is famous for its rare and endemic wildlife, specifically the Assam Roofed Turtle, Hispid Hare, Golden Langur, and the Pygmy Hog. It was once placed on the "World Heritage in Danger" list due to heavy poaching and militancy (Bodo insurgency) but was successfully removed from the danger list in 2011 after recovery.

questions.stem: Keibul Lamjao National Park is famous for being the world's only floating national park. Which endangered deer species is exclusively found here?

options.option_text: Sangai (Brow-antlered deer)
Hangul (Kashmir Stag)
Barasingha (Swamp deer)
Chinkara (Indian Gazelle)

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Keibul Lamjao National Park is located on the Loktak Lake in Manipur. It is an integral part of the lake, composed of floating decomposed plant materials called 'phumdis'. It is the last and only natural habitat of the endangered Sangai (Rucervus eldii eldii), also known as the brow-antlered deer or "dancing deer" (because it appears to dance as it walks on the unstable, bobbing phumdis).
DECOY BUSTING: Hangul is found exclusively in Dachigam National Park (Kashmir). Barasingha is famously the state animal of Madhya Pradesh (Kanha NP) and UP (Dudhwa NP). Chinkara is an antelope found in arid regions like Rajasthan.
EXAM INSIGHT: The Sangai is the state animal of Manipur. The construction of the Ithai Barrage has maintained high water levels year-round, preventing the phumdis from touching the lake bed during the dry season to absorb nutrients, thereby threatening the entire ecosystem.

questions.stem: Jim Corbett National Park, established in 1936 as India's first national park, was originally named after which British colonial official?

options.option_text: Sir Malcolm Hailey, then Governor of United Provinces
Lord Mountbatten, the last Viceroy of British India
Lord Curzon, Viceroy who partitioned Bengal in 1905
Lord Dalhousie, who introduced the Doctrine of Lapse policy

questions.explanation: When India's first national park was gazetted in 1936 in present-day Uttarakhand, it was named Hailey National Park after Sir Malcolm Hailey, Governor of United Provinces. It was renamed Ramganga National Park (1952) and finally Jim Corbett National Park (1957) to honour the conservationist hunter. Lord Curzon is the most tempting distractor since he was a vocal wildlife conservationist, but he was not the park's namesake.

questions.stem: Which Indian national park shares its mangrove ecosystem across India and Bangladesh, holds both UNESCO World Heritage Site and Ramsar Wetland designations, and shelters the world's largest mangrove-dwelling tiger population?

options.option_text: Bhitarkanika National Park in the Mahanadi delta, Odisha
Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary in the Godavari delta, Andhra Pradesh
Sundarbans National Park in the Bengal delta, West Bengal
Keoladeo Ghana National Park in Bharatpur district, Rajasthan

questions.explanation: Sundarbans National Park (West Bengal) is the world's largest contiguous mangrove forest, straddling both India and Bangladesh. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987 and is a Ramsar Wetland, hosting 100+ Royal Bengal Tigers adapted to saline tidal habitats. Bhitarkanika is a classic distractor — it is also a major delta mangrove sanctuary in India — but it does not extend into Bangladesh and is not a UNESCO WHS.

questions.stem: Kanha National Park in Madhya Pradesh is credited with rescuing which subspecies of deer from the brink of extinction — its wild population having fallen below 100 individuals before targeted conservation reversed the decline?

options.option_text: Kashmiri Red Stag (Hangul) found in Dachigam Reserve, J&K
Hard-ground Barasingha, a subspecies endemic to Kanha's meadows
Manipur Brow-antlered Deer (Sangai) of Keibul Lamjao wetlands
Persian Deer (Chinkara) found across arid grasslands of Rajasthan

questions.explanation: The Hard-ground Barasingha (Cervus duvaucelii branderi) is a subspecies uniquely adapted to dry, firm ground — unlike its swamp-dwelling Terai relatives. Its population collapsed to fewer than 100 by the 1970s due to habitat loss and hunting. Kanha's strict protection programme raised numbers to several hundred. Option C (Sangai) is the strongest distractor — it is equally rare and equally iconic — but it is endemic to Manipur's Keibul Lamjao, not Kanha.

questions.stem: The Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary in Kerala was formed around the reservoir of which dam, whose ongoing inter-state water-sharing dispute between Kerala and Tamil Nadu has remained a long-standing Supreme Court constitutional issue?

options.option_text: Idukki Arch Dam on the Periyar River in Idukki district
Mullaperiyar Dam built by British engineers in 1895 in Kerala
Banasura Sagar Dam on the Karamanathodu River in Wayanad
Parambikulam Dam on the Parambikulam River in Palakkad district

questions.explanation: Periyar Lake — around which the sanctuary and tiger reserve are built — was created by the Mullaperiyar Dam, constructed in 1895 by British engineer John Pennycuick. Tamil Nadu controls the dam (on Kerala's territory) under a 999-year lease, making its safety and water levels a high-profile inter-state dispute litigated before the Supreme Court. The Idukki Arch Dam is the most tempting distractor because it is also on the Periyar River and is Kerala's largest dam, but it was built in 1976 — decades after the sanctuary was formed.

questions.stem: Which tiger reserve became the first in India to be completely emptied of its entire tiger population due to organised poaching, triggering a Supreme Court-directed overhaul of Project Tiger and eventual creation of the NTCA?

options.option_text: Sariska Tiger Reserve in the Aravalli hills of Rajasthan
Panna Tiger Reserve in the Vindhya ranges of Madhya Pradesh
Buxa Tiger Reserve in the Terai Duars region, West Bengal
Simlipal Tiger Reserve in the Eastern Ghats of Odisha state

questions.explanation: Sariska Tiger Reserve (Rajasthan) was confirmed tiger-free by 2004–05 after systematic poaching by the Sansar Chand network. The Supreme Court intervened, mandating the Sunita Narain-led Tiger Task Force whose recommendations led to the creation of the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) under the Wildlife Protection Amendment Act 2006. Panna (Option B) is the strongest distractor — it also lost all tigers (by 2009) and underwent successful reintroduction — but Sariska was the first and the catalyst for the institutional overhaul.

questions.stem: Namdapha National Park in Arunachal Pradesh is described as India's only protected area where four big cat species coexist within a single contiguous landscape. Which option correctly names all four?

options.option_text: Tiger, Leopard, Snow Leopard, and Fishing Cat across altitudinal zones
Lion, Tiger, Leopard, and Clouded Leopard across varied forest habitats
Tiger, Leopard, Snow Leopard, and Clouded Leopard in Namdapha's ranges
Tiger, Leopard, Cheetah, and Snow Leopard across the Patkai hill ranges

questions.explanation: Namdapha spans altitudinal zones from ~200 m to 4,500 m in the Eastern Himalayas/Patkai ranges, enabling four Felidae to occupy distinct niches: Tiger (lowland tropical forests), Leopard (mid-altitude subtropical), Snow Leopard (high-altitude rocky zones), and Clouded Leopard (lower subtropical/hill forests). The Fishing Cat (Option A) inhabits wetlands of Bengal and Odisha, not Namdapha. Cheetah (Option D) is functionally extinct in India and was never recorded in Namdapha. Lion (Option B) is restricted to Gir, Gujarat.

questions.stem: Gahirmatha Marine Wildlife Sanctuary in Odisha is the world's largest nesting ground for Olive Ridley sea turtles. What is the specific term for their remarkable synchronised mass-nesting phenomenon that occurs annually on these beaches?

options.option_text: Amplexus — the collective mating aggregation of marine reptiles
Arribada — the synchronised mass nesting of Olive Ridley turtles
Aggregation — a general seasonal gathering of turtles near coastal shores
Philopatry — the instinct of turtles to return to their birth beach

questions.explanation: Arribada (Spanish for 'arrival') is the precise term for the synchronised mass nesting in which thousands of Olive Ridley females come ashore simultaneously over a few nights. Gahirmatha, along with Rushikulya and the Devi river mouth, hosts the largest such events globally. Philopatry (Option D) is a real and related concept — turtles do use geomagnetic imprinting to return to natal beaches — but it describes the navigational behaviour, not the mass-nesting event. Amplexus refers specifically to the amplifying grip used by male amphibians during mating, not turtle nesting.
